hook_text: Two rooms, both covered by 12 square tiles. Do they need the same length of skirting board? Not even close.
clip_script: House plan in Gqeberha, drawn on grid paper. Area is the floor inside: count the squares. Kitchen, 4 by 3: 3 rows of 4, 12 square metres. A long passage, 6 by 2: also 12 square metres. Same area! Now the skirting board round the edge, that is perimeter. Kitchen: 4 plus 3 plus 4 plus 3, 14 metres. Passage: 6 plus 2 plus 6 plus 2, 16 metres. Same area, different perimeter. And a leaf on the grid? 12 full squares, 6 half squares make 3 more: about 15 square centimetres. Area: count the squares inside.
visual_style: Whiteboard grid plan with two rooms shaded in squares; skirting boards tracing their edges in a different colour; a leaf with half squares paired up.
pacing: Two rooms with equal area, the perimeter twist, then the leaf.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw three different rectangles that each cover 12 squares.
